html:
The Rivonia Trial was held in Pretoria from October 1963 to June 1964, in which ten leaders of the African National Congress and its armed wing were tried for sabotage and plotting against the state.

Police had raided Liliesleaf farm in Rivonia, near Johannesburg, in July 1963, seizing documents on the armed struggle of Umkhonto we Sizwe. Nelson Mandela, already in prison, was added to the accused. From the dock he gave a speech ending with the words that he was prepared to die for the ideal of a free society.

Eight men, among them Mandela, Walter Sisulu and Govan Mbeki, were sentenced to life imprisonment and most were sent to Robben Island. The trial drew world attention and silenced the ANC inside the country for years.
sum: The Rivonia Trial was held in Pretoria from October 1963 to June 1964, in which ten leaders of the African National Congress and its armed wing were tried for sabotage and plotting against the state.
